title: The Hidden Cost of Digits: Number Normalization and WER in ASR Systems
abstract: arXiv:2609.21084v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Modern automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems trained on extremely large datasets can produce transcripts with numbers written in Arabic numerals. This creates a need for fair comparison with models that output verbatim texts and proper processing of reference transcripts. Popular approaches often reduce text normalization to lowercase and remove punctuation, with no additional normalization applied to languages other than English. In this work, we analyze the impact of normalization of numerical expressions in the evaluation of ASR systems in various languages, using Polish as an example of a highly inflective language. We perform experiments on VoxPopuli and The Polish Parliamentary speech datasets and estimate word error rate (WER) differences for different text normalization approaches. We show that the difference due to the lack of number normalization in WER may be substantial - more than 2 percentage points, and often higher

translated_title: 数字的隐性代价：ASR系统中的数字规范化与WER
translated_abstract: 在超大规模数据集上训练的现代自动语音识别（ASR）系统可以生成以阿拉伯数字书写数字的转录文本。这就产生了与输出逐字文本的模型进行公平比较的需求，以及对参考转录文本进行适当处理的需求。流行的方法通常将文本规范化简化为小写化和去除标点符号，而对英语以外的语言不进行额外的规范化。在这项工作中，我们分析了数字表达式规范化对多种语言ASR系统评估的影响，并以波兰语作为高度屈折语的例子。我们在VoxPopuli和波兰议会语音数据集上进行了实验，估计了不同文本规范化方法下的词错误率（WER）差异。我们表明，由于缺乏数字规范化而导致的WER差异可能相当可观——超过2个百分点，且往往更高。
tldr: 该研究揭示了ASR系统评估中被忽视的数字规范化问题，表明在波兰语等高度屈折语言中，缺乏数字规范化可导致词错误率（WER）差异超过2个百分点。
en_tdlr: This study reveals the overlooked issue of number normalization in ASR evaluation, showing that the lack of number normalization can cause WER differences of more than 2 percentage points, especially in highly inflective languages like Polish.
